tasks.commitBody:
On /event/[id] program rows are the primary shape, and a program_item's edition reference is required — yet when the collective-wide edition read could not name it (truncated past the 500 cap, or the edition unreadable or deleted), the row fell to the terminal else and claimed 'No pinned edition': a statement of absence that a program row cannot express. #321/#329/#331 removed this family of stated negatives on repertoire rows; this was the one row shape none of the three covered, split out of #331's review.

The exclusion was a single line: the shared editionUnknown() predicate gated both feeds to kind:'repertoire' before any logic ran. The per-row truncated flag already rode program rows since #331. The fix narrows the gate on the reader feed only: a program row with a non-empty editionId whose label nothing resolves takes the unknown wording — unconditionally, since the reader's unnameable-pin rule never needed truncation, which is also why one edit covers both the truncated read and the complete-read dangling pin. A program row with no editionId stays false on both feeds (it cannot pose the zero-options question), and the editor feed is byte-identical: a program row carries no pin control, structurally.

Acceptance is wire-driven on both pages — truncation flows through the real deriveListRead from a count above the returned entities, never a hand-set flag — and the provisional spec that pinned the gap as-is is replaced by the rule.

Closes #337

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)

The agenda header carried the selected collective's name and, beside it, a link to a separate /collectives page whose whole purpose was choosing from a list — a 47-line scaffold whose own comment called it provisional, whose every string was hardcoded English, and which duplicated four of its five states from branches the agenda already renders localized. The one thing the dead page did better — naming WHICH databases failed the marker check — moves into the agenda's error branch as a parameterized message in all four locales, and that branch's link becomes what it always should have been: a retry that re-runs discovery rather than a navigation.

Switching from the header is the same code path the old flow ended in: selectCollective always updated the store and re-wrote the URL in place, and every cross-collective reset on the agenda hangs off the store-value effect, not the page lifecycle — verified against each guard in the #297/#299/#325/#326/#331 family, and pinned by tests that drive the real select through single and double switches. The known unguarded path — the RSVP saved-cue reconcile documented at the savedEventIds reset, bounded by Entu event-id uniqueness — is not fixed here (its own comment rules that a separate change); the header picker is recorded on it as a third condition, per the issue's requirement that gaps be reported rather than silently inherited. The #334 offline-cache partition constraint is likewise recorded at the switch site.

Closes #338

tasks.commitBody:
Mihkel reported the Links page unstyled twice, and both reports were right about different things. #335 fixed the first cause — every control was classless and invisible. This is the second: Links was the only route that never adopted the house page shell. The layout renders children unwrapped, every route supplies its own root, and Links supplied a bare flex column — no <main>, no page ground, no padding, no width limit — so content sat flush to the screen edge and the fields spanned the whole phone.

The fix is the three-layer idiom the library, admin and profile pages already open with, matched character-for-character against the library page (the closest analogue — a list surface with a create form): the page shell 'min-h-screen bg-paper px-6 py-10 text-ink', the centred 'max-w-md' column, and the heading moved from body-text styling to the house 'font-display text-2xl'. Contents are wrapped, not restyled — every control keeps the classes #335 gave it, and all five existing Links suites pass unchanged.

On the issue's open question of a shell guard: the route-root audit found the exceptions are real but enumerable — the agenda's conditional DeskSurface wrap, the centered auth/invite family, and auth/logout which renders nothing at all — while the issue's 'roster nests inside another container' turned out stale at HEAD (roster matches the library idiom byte-for-byte). A per-route allowlist guard (each route declares which of the known shell families it uses; the spec asserts the match) would be honest about the exceptions, at the cost of one allowlist entry per new route. Recorded here rather than built, per the issue.

Closes #339
